questions.q: What physical action does the child perform repeatedly in the opening stanzas of Rabindranath Tagore's poem "Paper Boats"?
questions.a: The child floats paper boats down the running stream one by one. A wrong answer—such as saying the child is building a bridge or sailing a real boat—shows a failure to recall the core visual imagery of the poem's opening lines, confusing the narrative action with other outdoor childhood games.

questions.q: When the child writes their name and village on each paper boat, what is the underlying intention or hope behind this action?
questions.a: The child hopes that someone in a strange, distant land will find the boat and discover who sent it, establishing a connection across space. A wrong answer—such as thinking the child is mailing letters to the local post office—shows a misunderstanding of the imaginative play, missing how the child yearns for unknown friends in faraway places.

questions.q: If a student summarizes the poem by stating, "The poem is only about a child playing with water during the rainy season," why is this summary incomplete?
questions.a: Steps: (1) Identify the literal event (playing with water). (2) Identify the imaginative and emotional layer (loading flowers, writing names, dreaming of distant shores). (3) Recognize that summary requires capturing both the physical action and the emotional theme. (4) Conclude that a complete summary must include the child's longing for connection, not just the outdoor play. A wrong answer indicates the student is struggling to look beyond the literal surface text into symbolic meaning.

questions.q: How does the progression of loading the boats with "shiuli flowers" from the garden deepen the summary of the child's inner thoughts?
questions.a: The flowers represent the best gifts the child has to offer, symbolizing sincerity, beauty, and the hope that these offerings will bloom safely in the night sky or distant lands. A wrong answer suggests the student views the flowers as mere litter or garbage, missing the emotional significance of the child giving away their garden treasures to unknown receivers.

questions.q: Evaluate whether the ending of "Paper Boats" presents a sense of despair or enduring hope. Justify your answer using the summary of the poem.
questions.a: The poem presents enduring hope because even as night falls and sleep approaches, the child dreams of their paper boats dancing on midnight stars and waking up to find future friends. A wrong answer arguing for despair fails to account for the uplifting, dreamy tone of the final stanzas where the child's imagination conquers distance and darkness.

questions.q: Write a concise three-sentence summary of "Paper Boats" that captures both the physical storyline and the central emotional theme of the poem.
questions.a: A strong answer must mention: (1) The child floating paper boats down a stream, (2) writing their name and village on them with hopes of being found, and (3) the concluding dream of night-time skies carrying those hopes forward. A poor answer is merely a single sentence listing random words or describing unrelated rain scenes from Class 6 stories.
